newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Thakral sees further profit gains.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Thakral sees further profit gains.

text.p: Hotel ownwer and management company, Thakral Holdings Ltd said on Thursday the company's performance to date had strengthened its foundation for improved profitability.
The company earlier announced that its net profit had risen 13 percent to A$15.4 million for the year to June 30, 1996.
"We expect our hotels will continue to perform strongly. Occupancy is still high," Thakral's managing director, David Conners told reporters in Sydney.
Conners said Thakral was now focusing on yield management to improve its hotel's earnings.
"We find that if you can get the room rates up this flows directly through to the bottom line," Conners said.
Thakral, part of the Thakral Group of Singapore, is the largest hotel owner in Australia, owning 2,143 rooms and managing 2,300 rooms under its subsidiary, All Season Hotels.

Conners said Thakral was looking at making further hotel acquisitions following its A$26.25 million purchase of the Pacific Bay Resort in Coffs Harbour on the north coast of New South Wales during its last financial year.
Asked if Thakral would consider buying a hotel in Sydney before the 2000 Olympic Games, Conner said: "We like hotels in growth areas."
Conner said Thakral was well positioned to take advantage of rising occupancy rates and rising room rates.
"Demand is still strong and supply is slow in coming on. We see the hotel market as very strong and we are well positioned to take advantage of that," he said.
At 3.40 p.m. (0540 GMT), Thakral shares were two cents firmer at 76 cents.
